Are the Mountaineers motivated? To become bowl eligible, West Virginia (5-5, 2-5 Big 12) must beat either UH or Utah. The Cougars might offer the Mountaineers' best chance. In two seasons at UH, Weigman has accounted for 68 total touchdowns, which leads all Power Four quarterbacks during that span. Weigman is 17-6 as UH's starter, the fifth-most wins nationally. Weigman has been especially careful with the ball with only three interceptions, including two on pass deflections. He's also lost a fumble on a strip-sack in each of the Cougars' losses. "He's had a great season, he really has," Fritz said. "He's kind of going up the draft boards, which is very, very deserving. We want to make sure he goes out a winner here." item.title: 2026 NCAA Women’s Soccer Tournament: Purdue 4, Southern Illinois 0
item.description: ST LOUIS, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 5: Irene Campo #14 of the Purdue Boilermakers celebrates with teammates after scoring the game winning goal against the Penn State Nittany Lions in extra time of the quarterfinals round of the 2026 Big Ten Soccer Championship at Energizer Park on November 5, 2026 in St Louis, Missouri. (Photo by Jeff Curry/Big Ten/University Images via Getty Images) Purdue’s return to the women’s NCAA soccer Tournament will last a bit longer. This afternoon the Boilers kicked off the entire tournament with the opening match of the whole show. They also left little doubt as they moved on with a dominant 4-0 win over Southern Illinois. This was a match where Purdue controlled possession and was never seriously threatened throughout. In fact, Southern Illinois didn’t even have a shot in the first half compared to 14 by Purdue. The Boilers got goals from McKenzie Carle in the 18th minute and Tanna Schornstein in the 26th minute to hold a comfortable 2-0 lead at halftime. The second half saw Irene Campo get a brace with goals at the 52nd and 67th minute, giving her a hand in all four Purdue goals after she assisted on both in the first half This continued Purdue’s dominant run over the past few weeks that has seen it become the best offensive team in the nation. Coming into today’s game Jaiden Anderson was the country’s leading goalscorer with 20 and as a team Purdue’s 74 goals was the best in Division I. Purdue now awaits the winner of tonight’s other first round match between 5 seed Texas and Houston. 1 seed Ohio State wins their opening match I believe the second round match would be played in Columbus next weekend, as the Buckeyes would host both second round matches and the Sweet 16 match with the way the bracket lines up. Purdue fell to the Buckeyes 2-1 earlier this season for one of just two losses it has suffered all year.

item.title: Fan Attending Cowboys-49ers Game Dies Days After Falling During In-Stadium ‘Altercation’
item.description: AT&T Stadium - Home to the Dallas Cowboys Credit: Nicole Cordeiro NEED TO KNOW A football fan died days after being involved in a fight at the Dallas Cowboys’ AT&T Stadium Mario Narro, 36, died on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at an Arlington, Texas hospital Narro fell during a fight before kickoff, but stayed to watch most of the game before he sought medical attention A 36-year-old man has died days after he was involved in a fight with another fan at a Dallas Cowboys game. Mario Narro died on Wednesday, Nov. 18 in the ICU at Medical City Arlington Hospital, according to the Tarrant County Medical Examiner and NBC 5 . His cause of death is currently pending, according to the ME’s office. Narro’s family members told the Arlington Police Department that he fell during an altercation at AT&T Stadium before kickoff, but that Narro stayed to watch most of the game between the Cowboys and the San Francisco 49ers before he began to complain of discomfort, according to NBC 5. AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Tx. Credit: typhoonski / Getty Images A friend alerted stadium paramedics who then worked to transport him to the local hospital, KERA News reported . Narro’s family submitted a police report on Nov. 17, the day before he died on Wednesday morning. The APD has opened an investigation into Narro’s death, and is reviewing surveillance from the stadium, per NBC 5. The NFC rivalry game, which featured a hearty contingent of Niners fans, was the site of numerous fights on Sunday. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! On social media , one such fracas involving two women went viral. The two fans wrestled on the ground of the stadium’s concourse as onlookers watched, while another fight between two men occurred in the background. The brawls occurred minutes after the game concluded, in which the 49ers beat up the home team, 46-40. The Cowboys next host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Read the original article on People

Coach Kevin O’Connell’s Minnesota Vikings are 7-2, tied for the NFC North lead, but have a huge task ahead of them with a road trip to Mexico City to play the 49ers on the docket. The Kyle Shanahan vs. Brian Flores coaching matchup looks like a high-level chess match , but the Vikings’ offense is also key with injuries rearing their ugly head. ESPN’s Adam Schefter shared the latest news on the Vikings’ offensive injuries, and it was a mixed bag for OC Wes Phillips’ group. “TJ Hockensen is off the Vikings injury report and good to go Sunday night,” he wrote. Cousins’ arrival has helped O’Connell’s team turn over a new leaf, adding to a passing game that needed better efficiency, leadership, accuracy, and big play potential. Murray’s stint with the Vikings has been a disappointing one health-wise and stats-wise, but he has done his part to make O’Connell’s team a contender amid a rapidly shifting roster each week. The Houston Texans are now 4-6 on the season after stomping the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on “Thursday Night Football” in Week 11 thanks to another solid outing from quarterback C.J. Stroud. While the 25-year-old signal-caller has yet to sign a contract extension with the club, he is at least doing his part to keep the team competitive. After another good game, Colin Cowherd couldn’t help but compare Stroud to Joe Burrow . Cowherd’s comparison had more to do with the contract situation for Burrow right before he signed his five-year, $275 million extension. The popular sports analyst claims that the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t do enough to build around Burrow before giving him his extension, and feels Stroud is in a similar situation with the Texans. “C.J. Stroud has had a great season, and now the Texans are trapped,” Cowherd said… “I feel like he’s going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn’t get it done enough before he signed the big deal.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "C.J. Stroud has had a great season and now the Texans are trapped… I feel like he's going to be Joe Burrow. They just couldn't get it done enough before he signed the big deal." @colincowherd on C.J. Stroud & the Texans pic.twitter.com/Of7YQ5dM0Y — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) November 20, 2026 The Texans initially went into the 2026-27 campaign believed to have the best defense in football, while questions surrounded Stroud about whether or not he is a franchise quarterback. Fast forward to Week 11, and the storyline is seemingly the opposite. Even though Houston has struggled throughout the campaign, the four-year veteran is putting up solid numbers, throwing for 2,656 yards, 22 touchdowns, and four interceptions with a 64.0% completion percentage through 10 games. Stroud is well on pace to throw for the most touchdowns in a single season in his career, as he’s just one shy of tying his career record of 23 set in his rookie year. If the defense can somehow get to the level of play it was last season, then the Texans could be a huge problem in the back end of the 2026-27 campaign. C.J. item.title: Knicks superfan Ben Stiller recalls losing his mind over Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. Pistons in 2025 playoffs
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images. Knicks superfan Ben Stiller recalls losing his mind over Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. Pistons in 2025 playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the most memorable moments of New York Knicks superfan Ben Stiller was Jalen Brunson’s game-winner vs. the Detroit Pistons during the 2025 playoffs. A fan responded to a post asking what the “greatest” non- OG Anunoby tip-in play in Knicks history was. One fan responded with a clip of Brunson’s game-winner in Game 6 of the Knicks-Pistons series last year, saying, “This s**t literally made Me lose my mind,” to which Stiller replied, “Me too.” Me too. https://t.co/NiNxCoU521 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Ben Stiller (@BenStiller) November 20, 2026 The play was huge. The game was tied at 113 before Brunson hit his three-pointer with about four seconds left in the game. Detroit was unable to score on their next possession. Brunson ended the game with 40 points. item.title: Juventus reignites interest in Manchester United star
item.description: Juventus reignites interest in Manchester United star Juventus are once again interested in signing Joshua Zirkzee as they look to strengthen their attacking options during the January transfer window. The Dutch striker was among their targets last summer when he was open to leaving Manchester United in search of regular playing time. The Bianconeri explored the possibility of signing him on loan, but they faced competition from several other clubs, including teams in the Premier League. At the time, Benjamin Sesko was identified as United’s preferred striker, which appeared to leave Zirkzee’s future uncertain. However, none of the potential moves materialised, giving Juventus another opportunity to pursue the forward. The Old Lady are keen to take advantage of the situation and could return with a fresh approach when the transfer window opens. Juventus revive their interest in Zirkzee Juventus regard Zirkzee as one of the attractive options available in the market and would like to bring him to Turin. Nevertheless, his situation at Manchester United could depend on the plans of Mauricio Pochettino, who has recently been appointed as the club’s manager. The Argentine will first need to assess the players available to him before making decisions about their respective futures. Zirkzee’s prospects could therefore become clearer once the new manager has evaluated his squad and decided which players fit into his plans. A decision from Pochettino could have an important influence on Juventus’ pursuit, particularly if the striker is allowed to leave in January. Bianconeri want attacking reinforcements According to Football Italia , Juventus remain interested in signing Zirkzee because they have not been satisfied with the performances of their current strikers. The report adds that Juventus intend to recruit a new forward in January, with the United attacker among the players they would particularly like to add to their squad. For Juventus, bringing in Zirkzee could provide another option in attack as they look to improve their attacking output . However, much will depend on Manchester United’s willingness to sanction his departure and whether Pochettino sees a future for the Dutchman at Old Trafford. A January move remains a possibility as Juventus continue to assess their options ahead of the transfer window.

item.title: Naomi Osaka issues statement as her 2026 season ends after ‘extreme eye-opener’ this year
item.description: Naomi Osaka’s 2026 season came to an end last month in front of a home crowd in Tokyo. The Japanese star played just 13 tournaments this year, including all four Grand Slams and six WTA 1000 events. But following the resurgent second half of her 2025 season, during which she made the semifinals of the US Open and the final of the Canadian Open, Osaka has not quite kicked on in 2026. While she reached the final in Bad Homburg and the quarterfinals of Wimbledon for the first time, the 29-year-old has not been able to rediscover the level that saw her win four Grand Slam titles from 2018 to 2021. Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Naomi Osaka releases statement on social media about her season In a post on Instagram , Osaka said: “Someone asked me for a season recap haha. This year has been an extreme eye-opener for me. I used to think I needed permission and approval to be myself, that I was weird for the things I wanted to express and create. “Turns out I was wrong, and the more I trusted my ideas and embraced my uniqueness, the happier and more fulfilled I became. This year is dedicated for anyone who feels a little different and is having a hard time navigating it- you’ll find yourself I promise.” Perhaps Osaka’s most impressive run in 2026 came at the Wimbledon championships, a tournament that, historically, she had struggled at. Prior to this season, Osaka had never made it past the third round of the grass court major across five appearances. But this year, Osaka made huge improvements on grass, reaching the final of the Bad Homburg Open without dropping a set. She was forced to retire during the championship match at the WTA 500 event against Karolina Muchova. Osaka’s impressive grass-court form continued into Wimbledon, where she reached the quarterfinals by beating then-world number one Aryna Sabalenka. Osaka was ultimately knocked out of the tournament by Muchova. After her run at Wimbledon, Osaka made the semifinals in Washington and the quarterfinals of the Canadian Open, but was beaten in the fourth round of the US Open by eventual champion Elena Rybakina. Osaka finished the year with an indifferent Asian swing and ended 2026 ranked 17th in the world, one spot lower than where she started the season.

Or maybe not. Between April and July, a span of 99 days, Costa stopped Stewart Nicoll, Matt Schnell and Cody Durden, each in under 10 minutes, and returns Saturday to close out the year on an ever higher note in Doha. The Albazi rematch is the fight he called for going into his clash with Durden, and the one he got after all. Winning in Qatar would make 2026 the best year of his MMA career, and Costa is willing to make an exception for his break if the UFC needs a backup fighter for the upcoming title bout between Joshua Van and Manel Kape, the headlining attraction for UFC 336 on Jan. 30 in Toronto. “My dream comes first, right?” Costa told MMA Fighting. “If I feel like an opportunity is going to come up, I’ll definitely be there, man. I’ll get some rest, but I’ll let them know, ‘If anything happens, I’m here. Just give me a call.’” “It seems like everything is going well [with Kape],” he continued. “He’s doing things differently now. He’s also a guy who struggles a little with his weight, but anything can happen. item.title: Arizona cross country prepared for uphill race at NCAA Championships
item.description: On Saturday the Arizona men’s cross country team will step up to the starting line with 31 other teams at the NCAA Championships. Competing at the championship meet is unfamiliar terrain for Arizona, a program that last made NCAA Championships in 2006. The course Arizona will be running on in Terre Haute, Indiana, however, is one the Arizona men — and women’s individual competitor Mercy Chepkemoi — are actually quite familiar with. That’s because Arizona competed last month at the Under Armor Pre-National Invitational, held at the LaVern Gibson Championship Cross Country Course in Terre Haute. Terre Haute, affectionally known in college cross country as Terradise, features one of the few courses specifically designed for the sport. According to Indiana State University, the course’s popularity is due to a mix of uphill and downhill sections that complement a simple straightaway start. Running up and down hills tests distance runners in ways than a relatively flat course doesn’t. It forces athletes to endure greater resistance (uphill) and navigate unique stresses (downhill). Arizona cross country coach Jay Koloseus said the team has worked all season on inclines in preparation for the type of course they’ll see Saturday. “Obviously we’re blessed to be close to the mountains here,” Koloseus said. “But it was also learning last year we were quite surprised we got to a course and it was very hilly.” When Arizona competed at the Pre-National Invitational in October, the team was less fearful for the LaVern Gibson course having done workout paces going up hills, Koloseus said. “I’m not going to say enjoyable, but it was really nice to see the athletes this year now that we’ve seen all the courses we’re going to see with big hills do their warmup run on it or practice the day before,” he said. “They all come back and say, ‘Wow, we’ve all done hills much worse than this,’ where last year we finished a few course jogs and you could see they were just kind of freaked out.“ The Arizona men took sixth at the Pre-National Invitational in a field that was competitive but not representative of what the Wildcats will face on Saturday. It’s possible the Jets’ thinking was that Hall might produce better after halftime if he was fresh and the defense was tired. In the end, the pair had similar rushing numbers, but Hall produced more as a receiver. You can probably expect the Jets to keep working on this with one option being flipping last week’s gameplan on its head and using Hall early, then keeping Allen fresh to be the hammer in the second half. The Chargers’ run defense did a great job against the Ravens, holding them to 16 yards on 15 carries, so it might not be easy to get a running game established. Will Daiyan Henley play? The Chargers’ leading tackler is linebacker Daiyan Henley, but he’s been managing a knee issue all season and has been missing practice this week. Henley, who is also second on the team in defensive snaps played, has been exploited in coverage at times this year, but is still a key contributor to the Chargers’ run defense and tends to be the guy who wears the defensive headset. If Henley can’t go, the next man up would be Marlowe Wax, who has played under 100 defensive snaps in his career. Can the Jets get to Herbert? Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has been struggling in the passing game. A large part of that is that the Chargers have struggled to protect him. item.title: Confidence meters for Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current ahead of NWSL final
item.description: Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/NWSL via Getty Images | NWSL via Getty Images The NWSL playoffs are down to the last two standing: the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current. One team has rode their home-field advantage and will have another chance to play in front of their supporters, while the visitors have momentum from taking down the 2026 NWSL Shield winners. Which finalist heads into the final with more confidence and as the favorite? How confident should the NWSL finalists be? 1. Washington Spirit | Semifinals: 2-1 win vs Utah Royals *Quarterfinals: 4-1 win vs Portland Thorns Confidence meter: 65% Washington advanced to their third straight NWSL Championship final, but is this the year they finally break through? Is the third time actually the charm? First off, the ‘Rowdy’ Audi crowd is sure to provide an unmatched home-field advantage for Adrián González’s side who had the easier path in the bracket. In two playoff matches, Washington has generated an xG of 4.08 (six goals scored) while conceding just 1.81 xG (two goals allowed). Forward Clara Luvanga now has six goal contributions in her last four games (three goals and three assists). With the home crowd and the form they are in, this is their best chance to bring home the trophy. The only question left, can the Spirit finish the job? 2. Kansas City Current | Semfinals: 2-1 win at Gotham FC *Quarterfinals: 1-0 win vs Angel City FC Confidence meter: 35% Kansas City took down arguably the most in-form team in the quarterfinals in Angel City FC and followed it up by knocking out the best team from the regular season, Gotham FC. By taking down the Bats, Kansas City showed they can handle a difficult road atmosphere despite a 5-9-1 away record in the regular season. In two playoff matches, the Current have generated 2.92 xG (three goals scored), and conceded 1.79 xG (one goal allowed). The scary part? Scoring has come from Michelle Cooper, Croix Bethune and Haley Hopkins. Two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga is due for a huge goal and she might just bury the difference maker in the final. item.title: Arsenal is fighting Tottenham for Brazilian teenager
item.description: Arsenal is fighting Tottenham for Brazilian teenager Arthur Dias is regarded as one of the finest young talents in South American football as he continues to impress with Athletico Paranaense in the Brazilian top flight. The 19-year-old has attracted considerable attention with his performances and is expected to become a target for several European clubs in the coming seasons. Tottenham have been working hard to secure his signature, having identified him as one of the most promising talents available in the transfer market. The Lilywhites believe he has the potential to strengthen their squad in the future and are keen to bring him to Europe, where he could continue developing. However, they are now facing increased competition, with Arsenal entering the race to sign the Brazilian youngster. The Gunners are also keen to secure his services and could be in a strong position to challenge their London rivals. RTI Esporte reports that Mikel Arteta’s side have joined the list of clubs pursuing Dias, whom they regard as one of the standout talents in the Brazilian top flight. Arsenal have identified him as an ideal addition to their squad and are working hard to make a move happen. Arsenal step up their pursuit of Dias The Gunners believe Dias has the potential to become an important player in their squad and are determined to compete for his signature. Their interest represents a setback for Tottenham, who had previously appeared to be among the leading contenders for his services. Arsenal are reportedly in a stronger position than Spurs to complete the deal, which could give them an advantage in the race. Their ambition to recruit promising young players also makes Dias an attractive target as they look to strengthen their options for the future. (Photo by Ricardo Moreira/Getty Images) Brazilian connection could prove important Another factor that could work in Arsenal’s favour is the presence of an established Brazilian centre back in their squad. Having someone familiar with Brazilian football and its culture could help Dias settle more comfortably if he decides to move to north London. The opportunity to develop at Arsenal, alongside an established Brazilian defender, could be particularly appealing to the teenager. The Gunners will hope this connection helps convince him that their project offers the right environment for his development. item.title: Colts Waive QB Daniel Jones: What It Means For Anthony Richardson Sr.
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 24: Anthony Richardson #5 of the Indianapolis Colts jumps in the air as he reacts during to an NFL preseason game at Lincoln Financial Field on August 24, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones. It’s been a subpar season for both Jones and the Colts. The Colts are 3-8 and Jones ranks near the bottom of the barrel in multiple categories. Jones threw just seven touchdowns in 11 games with 13 interceptions. After a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night with Jones completing just 12-of-27 passes for 144 yards and an interception, the Colts decided to make a major change. Jones, 29, signed a two-year extension with the Colts in March, with nearly $49.5 million of that guaranteed. With Jones now released, Colts head coach Shane Steichen announced that Anthony Richardson Sr. will start versus the New York Giants on Nov. 29. Anthony Richardson Gets Another Chance As Indianapolis Colts Starting QB Richardson was selected by the Colts with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, but his career has had ups and downs to this point. Richardson has thrown just six passes the last two seasons and has an 8-7 career starting record with 11 passing touchdowns, 13 interceptions and 10 rushing scores. Richardson is still just 24 years of age and there’s a chance his full potential has yet to be realized. With the Colts offensive line struggling, Richardson’s dual-threat capabilities could give the offense a boost. “I’m excited to see him play and go compete, and obviously he brings a unique skill set that’s very athletic and can run around and make some plays,” Steichen said . So, looking forward to seeing that.” Richardson is a free agent in March, and the Colts are a team that are in the midst of a rebuild and trying to figure out how they’ll look in 2027. The Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline and also traded offensive lineman Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. In short, the Colts have a largely depleted roster at the moment which is going to make it harder for the franchise and Richardson to succeed the rest of the season. Even if this isn’t the most ideal situation for Richardson to be thrust into as QB1, it’s better than no opportunity at all. If Richardson fares well, it’ll bode well for his future whether the Colts bring him back or he plays elsewhere next season. Steichen noted that Richardson has “matured a lot” between his rookie season and now and that a full week of practice reps as the starting quarterback will benefit him well. The Colts drafted him No. 4 overall in 2023 for a reason, and turning to Richardson once again as starting quarterback represents that they haven’t given up on his potential just yet. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Yankees 5-Player Trade Idea Dumps Anthony Volpe, Will Warren For Marlins Star
item.description: New York Yankees infielder Anthony Volpe The New York Yankees infield is a mess right now, and they may need to make a trade in order to fix it. Jazz Chisholm Jr. could be playing elsewhere next season. The Yankees have Anthony Volpe and Luis García Jr. as internal options to replace him, but they could look for better options. The Athletic's Jim Bowden proposed this trade that would net the Yankees Otto López from the Miami Marlins: Marlins receive: Jasson Domínguez, Anthony Volpe and Will Warren Yankees receive: Otto López and Agustín Ramírez López is a shortstop, but can also play second base. The Yankees could keep López at shortstop and move George Lombard Jr. to second base. Volpe would get a fresh start in Miami, playing next to Xavier Edwards. Ramírez would give the Yankees another option at catcher besides Wells. Another option for López on the Yankees would be playing third base to replace Ryan McMahon. The Yankees could then play García at second base, keeping him in the lineup regularly. As far as Domínguez and Warren go, the Yankees don't really need them. Warren is a solid pitcher, but the Yankees already have four All-Star-caliber starters. They have Cody Bellinger, Aaron Judge and Spencer Jones in the outfield, so Domínguez is expendable as well. The outfield and starting rotation are areas the Yankees can afford to deal from. López is under club control through 2029 and is coming off a season in which he was an All-Star and hit .305. item.title: Bayern's Kane and Olise subbed out with injury
item.description: Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane receives treatment for an ankle injury on Friday (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Bayern Munich forwards Harry Kane and Michael Olise were subbed out after picking up injuries in the first-half of Friday's home Bundesliga clash with Cologne. With 15 minutes gone, England captain Kane was felled from behind by Cologne defender Joel Schmied in the box. After a VAR review, the referee waved away Kane's claims of a penalty. The Ballon d'Or winner tried to continue despite a clear limp, but was subbed out shortly after. Kane, 33, has a history of ankle complaints although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. Olise went down after a tackle near the penalty arc late in the first-half. Despite continuing until the break, the France player did not return to the pitch for the second-half. The former Crystal Palace winger left the stadium during the second-half on crutches for further treatment. Any potential further absences would come at a bad time for Bayern who are in the midst of an injury crisis, particularly up front. Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies and captain Manuel Neuer have all missed matches recently, while coach Vincent Kompany returned to the dugout on Friday after missing a month with a meningeal irritation. Bayern are the only team in Europe's top-five leagues yet to lose in any competition this season. They travel to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. dwi/ea

They use their pre-conference slate to raise money via buy games against high-major teams. They’ve played the 8th-toughest schedule in the nation, with their only win coming in their lone home game against a similarly positioned mid-major. Basically, they’re losing basketball games on the road to fund their athletic department. I don’t see them as being much different than Valparaiso in terms of talent; in fact, Valparaiso is the perfect point of reference for Purdue fans. This team is built around two players: center Chris Fields and wing Nassim Mashhour. Valpo was built around two players: center JT Pettigrew and guard Rakim Chaney. The Boilermakers did a good job holding Pettigrew to 11 points (7 points below his season average) but couldn’t stop Rakim Chaney from going on a 35-point heater that will live on in Chaney family lore for generations. There’s no way Chaney wasn’t at the top of Purdue’s defensive game plan. The only way for the Beacons to come into the Mackey and leave with a victory was for their best player to do something exceptional, and yet, the Boilermaker defense looked surprised every time the ball went through the net. I’ve said this for multiple seasons, but I’m not sure I’ve ever seen a program so consistently bad at handling a hot player. If Purdue gets the ball out of Chaney’s hands, they win. I don’t understand why Coach Painter didn’t send an instant double and see if anyone else on the Beacons had the nerve to take big shots, but I digress. My point is that Oakland presents the exact same challenge. They have one interior player (Fields) and one perimeter player (Mashhour) who do the majority of their scoring. Mashhour is a balanced wing, shooting 37% from 3 and 42% from 2 while drawing 37 fouls and shooting 92% from the free-throw line. He’s the type of player who loves attack closeouts but won’t hesitate to pull the trigger from deep if the closeout is late. Remember, his early season stats are legit. He put up 15 last time out against Arizona State in his lowest-scoring game of the season. He put up 28 on Boise State, shooting 5/11 from deep and hitting all 9 of his free-throw attempts. The only way Purdue loses this game is if Mashhour goes nuclear, which is the same proposition they faced against Rakim Chaney. I’ll be interested to see if the coaching staff makes any adjustments to their defensive strategy tonight. With Mashhour taking care of things on the perimeter, Fields can focus his attention on the paint. He’s averaging a double-double against the 8th-toughest schedule in the nation. He went 17-for-11 against Arizona State, which included 8 free-throw attempts. He went 15-for-13 against Alabama, with another 7 free-throw attempts. He played 17 minutes and fouled out trying to guard Fields in the post and keeping him off the boards. Defty’s backup, 6’11”, 200-pound Jonathan Grisham, played 11 minutes and committed 4 fouls. This will be a major challenge for Daniel Jacobsen on the defensive end. Fields will give him every opportunity to commit a foul, and as we all know, getting Jacobsen off the court is one of the keys to beating this Purdue team. I don’t think Oakland has enough to win this game, but I’ll be watching how this team handles the challenge they couldn’t navigate against Valpo. The task is clear. Stop Masshour and Fields, and short of a horrific shooting performance from the Boilermakers (which isn’t completely out of the question), Oakland won’t be able to generate enough offense to win. If one of these two goes off, and they’re both capable, things might be more uncomfortable than some folks are anticipating. Antoine West wasn’t fully weaponized in the Valpo loss. He’ll keep Purdue out of danger with his scoring tonight.

item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’ve done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Tuesday’s final Nations League group match, at home to Kosovo, presents a chance for progress or yet another opportunity to showcase a frustrating habit of messing things up. For 78 minutes in Linz on Saturday, Heimir Hallgrímsson’s side gave as good as they got against an Austria side who had not lost at home for a little more than three years. Set up in a compact, attack-minded formation they carried credible threat against hosts managed by Ralf Rangnick, but to nobody’s great surprise Sasa Kalajdzic broke the deadlock, scrambling home the winner from a needlessly conceded and poorly defended corner. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
